summary: The machinery for combining a scene out of many files is standardized. What you put inside the scene is not. The alliance behind it has published exactly one document, the core, version 1.0.1, dated 2025-12-12, and its own public repository lists that single row under available specifications. The core covers data types, the layer document model, paths, resource resolution, composition, value resolution, schemas, colour, collections and three file formats. It excludes geometry, materials and physics by name, and the words geometry and physics each appear exactly once in the whole document, in the sentence that excludes them. Two things a standards audience should carry away. First, the only schemas the core normatively defines are colour and collections, so there is no agreed way to say how big something is or which way is up. Second, the document is published under a licence that forbids distributing derivative works, which constrains how another standards body can build on it. Cite version 1.0.1 and the date: there is no 1.0.0.
